chunks: On the earth are tracts adjoining one another, and vineyards, fields of corn and date-palm trees, some forked, some with single trunks, yet all irrigated by the self-same water, though We make some more excellent than the others in fruit. There are surely signs in them for those who understand.

key_terms.قِطَعٌ مُتَجَاوِرَاتٌ: tracts or plots of land adjoining one another
key_terms.لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ: for a people who use their reason

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the diversity of crops and water in the earth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a metaphor for the diversity of human intellect and spiritual capacity; just as crops share a single water source (divine revelation) but yield different fruits, individuals respond to the same truth according to their inner disposition. It underscores the concept of *ikhtilaf* (diversity) as a deliberate divine wisdom rather than a flaw, inviting reflection on how the same guidance produces varying degrees of understanding among people of intellect.
